detection.title: SSH brute-force (password guessing)
detection.plain: One address hammered the server with password guesses far faster than any human could type.
detection.action: Block the source IP; confirm no successful login from it; review lockout settings.
detection.severity_rule: Points: 2 if attempts >= 100, 1 if attempts >= 20; +1 if the peak 5-minute window >= 30 attempts; +1 if a privileged account was targeted. High at 4 or more points, Medium at 2 or 3, otherwise Low.

detection.title: Username enumeration / password spraying
detection.plain: One address tried a few passwords against many different usernames, hunting for any account that works.
detection.action: Block the source IP; check whether any targeted account exists and was accessed; enforce MFA or keys.
detection.severity_rule: High if 20 or more usernames were tried or a privileged account was targeted, otherwise Medium.

detection.title: Distributed attack on a single account
detection.plain: Many different addresses attacked the same account at once, which points to a botnet and defeats per-IP blocking.
detection.action: Add account-level throttling; restrict SSH to VPN or allow-list; per-IP blocking alone is insufficient.
detection.severity_rule: High if the account is privileged or 15 or more IPs took part, otherwise Medium.

detection.title: Successful login after repeated failures (possible compromise)
detection.plain: An address failed several times and then got in. Treat the account as possibly compromised until proven otherwise.
detection.action: Treat as possible compromise: isolate account, force credential reset, review session activity and persistence.
detection.severity_rule: Always Critical: a login succeeded after repeated failures.

detection.title: Reconnaissance / port scanning
detection.plain: An address connected repeatedly without attempting to log in, which is typical of scanning for open SSH services.
detection.action: Monitor; block if repeated; confirm port 22 exposure is intended.
detection.severity_rule: Always Low: probing without login attempts.

attacker_severity: An attacker IP takes the highest severity among the incidents raised against it. An IP that raised no incident is shown as 'No incident'. Severity is separate from the risk score.
risk_formula: Score = 100 x sum(weight x component), each component between 0 and 1. Weights: volume 0.30, intensity 0.20, breadth 0.15, persistence 0.15, privileged 0.10, invalid 0.10. An IP with a successful login after repeated failures is raised to at least 90. Tiers: Medium from 35, High from 60, Critical from 80.

risk_components.label: Volume
risk_components.meaning: How many failed attempts the IP made. Log scale, so 1,000 attempts reaches the cap.

risk_components.label: Intensity
risk_components.formula: min(1, peak attempts in any 5-minute window / 50)
risk_components.meaning: How fast the IP guessed at its fastest.

risk_components.label: Breadth
risk_components.meaning: How many different accounts the IP tried.

risk_components.label: Persistence
risk_components.meaning: How many different hours the IP was active.

risk_components.label: Privileged targets
risk_components.formula: share of attempts aimed at root, admin and other privileged accounts
risk_components.meaning: Attacks on powerful accounts count for more.

risk_components.label: Invalid usernames
risk_components.formula: share of attempts using usernames that do not exist on the server
risk_components.meaning: Guessing names is a sign of automated scanning.

anomaly_rule.label: Hourly attempts far above the same hour of the previous 7 days (robust z-score >= 5)
